narr: An upper trough situated from the Great Lakes through the Tennessee Valley provided the instability to support very slow-moving showers and thunderstorms that drifted across the central Appalachians into the lower Mid-Atlantic. During the afternoon of the 9th, a surface trough had developed from Surry County, NC northward through Montgomery County, VA into southeast West Virginia, providing the low level convergence needed to support prolonged thunderstorm activity. Southerly wind flow carried deep moisture northward from the Carolina coast during the afternoon, with precipitable water values near 1.5 inches across Surry County, while surface-based CAPE values were observed in the 1,000 to 1,200 J/Kg range. Steering winds were less than 10 knots from the south, leading to slow storm movement.
ev: Runoff from an estimated 3.5 to 4 inches of rainfall during a 1-hour period flooded a portion of Radar Road at least 6 inches deep near the intersection with Ararat Road, making the road impassible until the flooding receded. No damage was reported to the road, and it was reopened to traffic after the flooding ended.
